newsitem.title: RUSSIA: New Russian tax chief promises tough policies.
newsitem.headline: New Russian tax chief promises tough policies.

text.p: Alexander Pochinok, the new head of the Russian State Tax Service, said in an interview published on Thursday that taxes should be cut, but he warned Russians they faced tough penalties if they did not pay their bills.
"In my opinion the State Tax Service has adopted too mild a policy," Pochinok, previously head of a sub-committee in the State Duma lower house of parliament, told Kommersant Daily newspaper.

"We need to be much tougher... The moment a taxpayer has money and refuses to pay, we need to exact this money in a tough way. The tax service has to be strong enough to obtain what it is entitled to by law."

Pochinok, a member of the small reformist parliamentary group Democratic Choice of Russia, said Russia needed to lower the overall tax burden by around 25 percent and improve the system for collecting income tax.

Russia urgently needed an improved tax code, he said, adding that separate laws and decrees would be needed if it took a long time to adopt the code, which is supposed to form the legal basis underpinning future budgets.

"A state which does not know how to collect taxes, in which taxes are not paid and taxes are too high for the citizens and unfair, such a state is unviable," he said. "We have to do something to avoid finding ourselves in such a situation."

Ministers admit low tax revenues are among Russia's most pressing economic problems and First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Thursday that tax revenues were just 40 percent of planned levels in the first quarter.
Pochinok, clearly aware of rivalries between different branches of the Russian administration, said the tax service needed to cooperate closely with the central bank and the state customs committee.
He said tax arrears from big corporate debtors would be one of his priorities.

"It is time to clean out the Augean stables," he said. "If an enterprise does not work, does not pay taxes, it should be closed down. And new ones should be registered only in the locality where they actually operate."
